A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SHINE and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–L. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection establish correspondence across equations, figures, tables and supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, component ablations, cross-attention analyses, experiments with alternative backbones and a 50-participant user study.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–4 and the main-text and appendix figures, including the user study.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same non-inversion latent preparation, Manifold-Steered Anchor loss, Degradation-Suppression Guidance and Adaptive Background Blending, including the adapter and LoRA variants.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate DreamEditBench and ComplexCompo with the same represented subjects, resolutions and challenging composition scenarios. The appendix analyses and proprietary-model test scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 4 retain the same 11 baselines. Figure 2 retains Grok 4, Gemini 2.5, SeedEdit/Doubao and GPT-5. The newly cited works are not evaluated as comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and the appendices retain the same 220- and 300-pair benchmarks, metrics, model configurations and denoising settings. The user study still involves 50 participants completing 50 ranking tasks each.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 2 and Figure 7, blending analysis in Appendix B, attention-map analysis in Appendix D, failure cases in Figure 8 and identity-metric analysis in Appendix I are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same averaging practices for benchmark scores, attention-mask IoUs and user rankings. Neither introduces repeated-run or seed disclosures, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match. For example, Table 1 retains Ours-LoRA DreamSim scores of 0.3577 on DreamEditBench and 0.3542 on ComplexCompo, while Table 4 retains its average user-study rank of 1.52.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 and Appendix C's derivation concerning query blurring and attention-weight blurring are unchanged. No mathematical definitions, assumptions or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same SHINE components, ComplexCompo benchmark contribution and state-of-the-art image-composition claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of identity preservation, composition realism and metric shortcomings are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning incorrect inpainting colors and dependence on customization-adapter quality.

D1.justification: Implementation details, Table 5 hyperparameters and baseline repository links are unchanged. Both versions still promise public release of the code and benchmark, with no new access information.

R1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds citations to Gao et al. (2025), Revoking Amnesia, and Zhou et al. (2025c), DragFlow, with corresponding bibliography entries. These extend an existing general-applications citation list without changing the comparative discussion or novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Edits are confined to the citation callouts in Appendix A.2 and the first-page arXiv version/date stamp. The title, authors, substantive prose, terminology and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added references cause limited bibliography reflow across pages 12–19 and line wrapping in Appendix A.2. All figures, tables and captions retain their designs and positions.

improvement.justification: The two added citations modestly update related-work coverage without adding comparative analysis. Methods, evidence, interpretations, limitations and reproducibility information remain unchanged, leaving overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
